text:
[RTCT.7.3] **A `pump_wcet_ns` breach halts the tier.** Pump timing is measured
at pump completion. On a breach the engine **must** emit an `EngineError`
carrying `ENGINE_FAULT_PUMP_WCET` and halt the tier — rung 7 of [LERR.1] — and
**must** return `DS_ERR_CONTRACT_WCET_HALT` from the pump that breached. From
there the halt is every `EngineError`'s halt ([NCBK.2.9]): the integrator **must
not** resume service, the engine's state is undefined ([LERR.1.4.7]), and each
later call but the few that clause leaves valid is refused with
`DS_ERR_ENGINE_HALTED`.

**Exceeding the worst-case execution time is a system failure, not a refused
operation.** Ten of [RTCT.7.1]'s caps decide **before** the work happens, so
the operation does not begin and the engine is intact ([RTCT.7.2]). This one
decides **after**. The engine cannot interrupt a pump mid-execution, so by the
time the breach is known the tier has already missed the deadline it exists to
keep — and a real-time tier that has overrun is one whose timing contract no
longer holds, for that pump and for every pump after it. There is no state in
which continuing is safe, which is what puts this cap on rung 7 rather than
rung 2 ([LERR.1.5]).

**This cap reads a measurement, and it is the only one of the eleven that
does.** The other ten compare a count the engine holds; this one compares an
elapsed wall-clock time, which is a property of the host rather than of the
program. Two live runs of one event trace against one contract therefore
disagree about whether the cap was breached whenever their elapsed times fall
either side of it — a loaded host halts where an idle one does not. **No clause
promises that two live runs agree on this cap**, and one that did could not be
honoured by any engine.

**That is not a determinism failure, because [LDET.1.1] scopes the guarantee to
the event trace rather than to live reality.** Live execution is where the
measurement is taken; the trace is what the guarantee is about. Two live runs
at different speeds produce two different traces — one that halts here and one
that does not — and each replays faithfully as itself.

**A trace recording this fault ends with it**, because the tier halted: the
`EngineError` is the last record on the trace ([RFCS.3.1]). A replayer drives
the trace to that point, comparing every atom before it, and stops. The
terminal fault is the recorded run's cause of death rather than an observable
the replay must reproduce, so a replaying host that would not itself have
breached does not report a divergence ([LFST.9.2.1]).

```{admonition} This is the one recorded compare atom a replay does not compare
:class: warning
[LFST.9.3.1] forbids the compare acquiring an exclusion list, and this is not
one. An exclusion list narrows the comparison **within** a run that continues,
so the un-compared thing goes unnoticed while everything after it is still
checked. A terminal fault has nothing after it: the trace ends, and there is no
remainder whose verification it could weaken. The replay reports what it found
rather than passing over it.
```

**No requirement here is written against where a recording ends.** A recording
is evidence of how far one run got, and a run ends for reasons that are the
engine's and for reasons that are not; a host losing power mid-pump ends a trace
as surely as a fault does. Nothing in a recording attests that it is complete
([RFCS.19.8]), so a requirement written against its end would be a requirement
about the power supply.

idris.name: rtct_7_3__wcet_breach
idris.note: The pump_wcet_ns decision. Its first argument is not logical state -- it is the wall-clock time the pump took, measured at completion.

idris.name: rtct_7_3__wcet_breach_varies_with_the_host
idris.note: The wcet decision varies with the HOST: elapsed 5ns against a 3ns cap breaches, elapsed 1ns against the same cap does not, with the logical state identical by construction. That is why the breach is a halt rather than a refusal -- a decision the program does not determine cannot be one the engine carries on from. It refutes a property the corpus never granted: [LDET.1.1] scopes the guarantee to the trace, and two live runs produce two traces.
